object.title: Almost color-balanced perfect matching conjecture
object.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers, and let $c:E(K_{2kn})\to [k]$ be an edge-coloring such that every color class has the same number of edges. A perfect matching $M$ of $K_{2kn}$ has color-deviation measure

$$
f(M)=\sum\limits_{i=1}^k\Big||c^{-1}(i)\cap M|-n\Big|.
$$

**Almost color-balanced perfect matching conjecture.** There is a perfect matching $M$ of $K_{2kn}$ with

$$
f(M)\leq O(k^2).
$$

This conjecture asks for a perfect matching whose numbers of edges in the $k$ color classes are collectively within a bounded $O(k^2)$ deviation of the color-balanced target $n$ in each class. The paper proves the weaker bound $f(M)\leq 3k\sqrt{kn\ln(2k)}$ in general and proves the stronger bound $f(M)\leq 2$ when $k=3$, while the stated $O(k^2)$ bound remains unresolved.
object.source_name: Johannes Pardey and Dieter Rautenbach, “Almost color-balanced perfect matchings in color-balanced complete graphs”, arXiv:2105.05661 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: Infinitely many Ramanujan-type congruences for 3- and 5-regular partitions
object.statement:
Let $b_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-regular partitions of $n$, where $k\in\{3,5\}$, and let $m$ be a positive integer. A **Ramanujan-type congruence** is a congruence of the form

$$
b_k(An+B)\equiv 0\pmod m
$$

for suitable integers $A$ and $B$. **The 3- and 5-regular partition congruence conjecture.** For $k\in\{3,5\}$ and every positive integer $m$, there are infinitely many Ramanujan-type congruences modulo $m$.

The paper proves this assertion when $m$ is prime and $m\geq 5$; the conjecture extends the existence of infinitely many such congruences to every positive integer modulus.
object.source_name: Qi-Yang Zheng, “Distribution of 3-regular and 5-regular partitions”, arXiv:2205.03191 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

object.title: Hamiltonicity conjecture for weakly pseudorandom graphs
object.statement: Let a weakly $(n,\beta)$-graph be a graph in the sense defined in the source, and let $G$ be Hamiltonian when it contains a Hamilton cycle. **Hamiltonicity conjecture for weakly $(n,\beta)$-graphs.** There exists a constant $\beta>0$ such that every weakly $(n,\beta)$-graph with $n\ge 3$ (or sufficiently large $n$) is Hamiltonian. The source says this conjecture is stronger than the stated Krivelevich–Sudakov and Gu conjectures; its resolution is not given.
object.source_name: Xiaofeng Gu and Muhuo Liu, “A unified combinatorial view beyond some spectral properties”, arXiv:2205.15228 (2022).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2003–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1611.06401](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.06401), [arXiv:1206.4846](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.4846), [arXiv:math/0303084](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303084).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

object.title: Conjecture on small regular subgraphs with prescribed average degree
object.statement: Let $s\geq 3$ be an integer. For sufficiently large $n$, let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with average degree at least $d$, where $C\log\log n\leq d\leq n^{\frac{s-2}{s}}$. **Regular-subgraph conjecture.** There is a constant $C=C(s)$ such that $G$ contains an $s$-regular subgraph on at most $nd^{-\frac{s}{s-2}}(\log n)^C$ vertices. This strengthens the paper’s bound for subgraphs of average degree at least $s$ by requiring regularity. The source notes that the unrestricted existence case is the Erdős–Sauer problem, resolved by Janzer and Sudakov, while the full order bound remains conjectural.
object.source_name: Oliver Janzer, Benny Sudakov and István Tomon, “Small subgraphs with large average degree”, arXiv:2207.02170 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02170

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2022).

object.title: The explicit limit conjecture for L(2)
object.statement:
Let $L(w)$ denote the lexicographically least infinite word on $\mathbb{N}$ beginning with $w$ whose only square factors are contained in the prefix $w$. Define the finite words $c_n$ recursively as in the paper, and let $\gamma$ be the morphism defined from the words $R_n$ and $b_n$ by

$$
\gamma(0)=c_3c_3^+,
$$

and, for $n\geq 0$,

$$
\gamma(n)=R_4b_4^+\;R_5b_5^+\cdots R_{n+2}b_{n+2}^+\;R_{n+3}b_{n+3}.
$$

**The explicit limit conjecture for $L(2)$.**

$$
L(2)=2\lim_{n\to\infty}c_n=2\gamma(L(\varepsilon)).
$$

This is the explicit version of the proposed structure of $L(2)$; it identifies the conjectured suffix both as the limit of the recursively constructed words $c_n$ and as the image of $L(\varepsilon)$ under $\gamma$.
object.source_name: Siddharth Berera, Andrés Gómez-Colunga, Joey Lakerdas-Gayle, John López, Mauditra Matin, Daniel Roebuck, Eric Rowland, Noam Scully and Juliet Whidden, “The lexicographically least square-free word with a given prefix”, arXiv:2210.00508 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.00508

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: The ordered linear sumset conjecture
object.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ have positive upper Banach density, and let $\ell,m\in\mathbb{N}$. For an increasing sequence $B=\{b_1<b_2<\cdots\}$, consider the ordered linear configuration

$$
\{\ell b_i+m b_j:i<j\}.
$$

**Ordered linear sumset conjecture.** There exist an infinite increasing set $B=\{b_1<b_2<\cdots\}\subset\mathbb{N}$ and an integer $t\geq0$ such that

$$
\{\ell b_i+m b_j:i<j\}\subset A-t.
$$

This is the linear case of the paper's ordered polynomial sumset questions. The source presents it as a conjecture motivated by partition regularity, while examples show that the ordering restriction matters.
object.source_name: Bryna Kra, Joel Moreira, Florian K. Richter and Donald Robertson, “Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond”, arXiv:2311.06197 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06197

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2023). “The case $k=2$ of , which corresponds to a slight variation of , is proved in .”

object.title: Hilton–Milner characterization conjecture for intersecting sets in 3-transitive groups
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-transitive permutation group of degree $n$. Two elements of $G$ are intersecting when they agree on at least one point, and an **intersecting set** is a subset $S\subseteq G$ whose elements are pairwise intersecting. A **canonical intersecting set** is a coset of a point stabilizer.

**Hilton–Milner characterization conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c_{0}<1$ such that, if $S$ is an intersecting set in $G$ satisfying

$$
|S|\geq c_{0}|G|/n,
$$

then $S$ is a subset of a canonical intersecting set in $G$.

This proposes a uniform stability-type description for sufficiently large intersecting sets, extending Hilton–Milner phenomena known for several particular permutation groups. The source does not report a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Venkata Raghu Tej Pantangi, “All 3-transitive groups satisfy the strict-EKR property”, arXiv:2311.13055 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.13055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

object.title: The 2-forest conjecture for even-hole-free graphs
object.statement: For an integer $k\geq 1$, a **$k$-forest** is a $K_{k+2}$-free chordal graph; in particular, a $2$-forest is a $K_4$-free chordal graph. An **even-hole-free** graph has no induced cycle of even length at least four, and an $(\mathcal{F})$-free graph contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a graph in $\mathcal{F}$. **The 2-forest conjecture.** Given an integer $t\geq 4$ and a $2$-forest $H$, every $(\text{even-hole},K_t)$-free graph of sufficiently large treewidth contains $H$ if and only if $H$ is a $2$-forest. The only-if direction follows from layered wheels; the substantive if direction is the main open question and is equivalent to the paper's main conjecture.
object.source_name: Sepehr Hajebi, “Chordal graphs, even-hole-free graphs and sparse obstructions to bounded treewidth”, arXiv:2401.01299 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01299

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2024). “This refutes Conjecture as well.”

object.title: The powers-of-sets containment conjecture
object.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $\delta>0$. For a finite set, density means cardinality divided by the cardinality of the ambient set. The notation $[n]^d$ denotes the $d$-fold Cartesian product of $[n]$, and $\mathcal{P}([n]^d)$ denotes its power set. **The powers-of-sets containment conjecture.** For $n$ sufficiently large depending only on $d$ and $\delta$, every subset $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}([n]^d)$ of density at least $\delta$ contains distinct subsets $A,B\subseteq[n]^d$ such that $A\subset B$ and

$$
B\setminus A=S^d
$$

for some subset $S\subset[n]$. This is the opposite-end specialization of the preceding conjecture when $k=2$; the source presents it as a remaining conjecture, so its general status is open.
object.source_name: Thomas Karam, “Unions of intervals in codes based on powers of sets”, arXiv:2408.15144 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15144

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2024). “The case $k=2$ is an important step towards Conjecture because it is still open while at the same time avoiding the extra difficulties coming from arithmetic progressions that arise for $k \ge 3$.”

object.title: Versteegen's even-decomposability conjecture
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with an even number of edges. It is **even-decomposable** if there is a sequence

$$
V(H)=V_0\backslash V_1\backslash\cdots\backslash V_k=\emptyset
$$

with each induced graph $H[V_i]$ having an even number of edges and $V_i\backslash V_{i+1}$ an independent set in $H$. Let $r_H(n)$ denote the least number of colours in an edge-colouring of $K_n$ with no even-chromatic copy of $H$.

**Versteegen's conjecture.** We have

$$
r_H(n)=n^{\Omega(1)}
$$

if and only if $H$ is even-decomposable.

Versteegen proved the forward obstruction that even-decomposable graphs satisfy $r_H(n)=n^{\Omega(1)}$. Thus the conjecture asserts that this is the only obstruction to the sub-polynomial bound $r_H(n)=n^{o(1)}$; it remains open.
object.source_name: Fredy Yip, “A variant of the Erdős-Gyárfás problem for K_8”, arXiv:2409.16778 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16778

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

object.title: Square-root deficit conjecture for transversals in equi-n-squares
object.statement:
An **equi-$n$-square** is an $n\times n$ array filled with $n$ symbols, each appearing exactly $n$ times. A **transversal** is a collection of cells sharing no row, column, or symbol; its size is the number of cells. **Square-root deficit conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that every equi-$n$-square has a transversal with size at least

$$
n-C\sqrt{n}.
$$

This conjecture proposes the expected order of the optimal universal lower bound after Stein's conjecture was disproved. The paper proves a lower bound of the form $n-n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, while its construction gives examples with no transversal of size $n-(1/(2\sqrt{2})+o(1))\sqrt{n}$; determining the sharp constant remains open.
object.source_name: Debsoumya Chakraborti, Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Richard Montgomery and Teo Petrov, “Almost-full transversals in equi-n-squares”, arXiv:2412.07733 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

object.title: Feige's even-cover girth conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
object.statement:
Fix $k\geq 2$. Let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ hyperedges, and let an **even cover** be a collection of hyperedges whose vertex-degrees are all even; its length is its number of hyperedges.

**Feige's conjecture.** There exists a sufficiently large constant $C>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$ and every $\ell$, every such $H$ with

$$
m\geq Cn\left(\frac{n}{\ell}\right)^{k/2-1}
$$

has an even cover of length at most $O(\ell\log_2 n)$.

This conjecture proposes a smooth interpolation between the extremal threshold $m=n+1$ and the regime where many hyperedges force an even cover of logarithmic length. The survey gives prior bounds but no resolution of the conjecture.
object.source_name: Benny Sudakov, “Restricted subgraphs of edge-colored graphs and applications”, arXiv:2412.13945 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13945

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024). “However, Euler's conjecture resisted solution for another 60 years until Parker, Bose, and Shrikhande in 1960 constructed mutually orthogonal Latin squares for all orders $n \geq 7$, showing that Euler's conjecture is false.”

object.title: Keevash–Mubayi–Sudakov–Verstraëte rainbow-cycle conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a properly edge-colored graph on $n$ vertices, meaning that no two edges incident with the same vertex have the same color. A **rainbow cycle** is a cycle whose edges all have distinct colors.

**Keevash–Mubayi–Sudakov–Verstraëte conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that every properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph with at least $Cn\log n$ edges contains a rainbow cycle.

The statement is motivated by a construction with $\Omega(n\log n)$ edges and is presented as the conjectured sharp order of magnitude. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Benny Sudakov, “Restricted subgraphs of edge-colored graphs and applications”, arXiv:2412.13945 (2024).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2401.10865](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10865).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13945

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024). “However, Euler's conjecture resisted solution for another 60 years until Parker, Bose, and Shrikhande in 1960 constructed mutually orthogonal Latin squares for all orders $n \geq 7$, showing that Euler's conjecture is false.”

object.title: Tan et al.'s conjecture on co-edge-regular graphs with four eigenvalues
object.statement: Let $G$ be a connected $k$-regular graph with $n$ vertices and co-edge-regular with parameter $\mu$, having four distinct eigenvalues. Let $t\geq 2$ be an integer. **Tan et al.'s conjecture.** There exists a constant $n_t$ such that, if $\theta_{min}(G)\geq -t$, $n\geq n_t$ and $k<n-2-\frac{(t-1)^2}{4}$, then either $G$ is the $s$-clique extension of a strongly regular graph for $2\leq s\leq t-1$, or $G$ is a $p\times q$-grid with $p>q\geq 2$. The conjecture seeks a Neumaier-type classification for co-edge-regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues; the cited spectral characterizations of clique extensions motivate it, but no resolution is supplied here.
object.source_name: Hong-Jun Ge and Jack H. Koolen, “On co-edge-regular graphs with 4 distinct eigenvalues”, arXiv:2503.12025 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12025

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2025).

object.title: Polynomial χ-boundedness conjecture for bounded merge-width classes
object.statement: A graph class is **χ-bounded** if there is a function $f$ such that every graph $G$ in the class satisfies $\chi(G)\leq f(\omega(G))$, where $\chi(G)$ is the chromatic number and $\omega(G)$ is the clique number. It is **polynomially χ-bounded** if $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial. **Polynomial χ-boundedness conjecture for bounded merge-width classes.** Every class of graphs with bounded merge-width is polynomially χ-bounded. Bounded merge-width classes are already known to be χ-bounded, and the conjecture asks for the stronger polynomial dependence on clique number. The stated paper proves χ-boundedness, but does not establish this polynomial strengthening.
object.source_name: Marthe Bonamy and Colin Geniet, “χ-Boundedness and Neighbourhood Complexity of Bounded Merge-Width Graphs”, arXiv:2504.08266 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08266

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

object.title: Narins–Pokrovskiy–Szabó conjecture on short leaf-to-leaf path lengths
object.statement: A **1–3 tree** is a tree in which every vertex has degree either $1$ or $3$. For a tree, a leaf-to-leaf path is a path whose endpoints are leaves. **Narins–Pokrovskiy–Szabó conjecture.** There exist a constant $\alpha>0$ and a function $N=N(n)$ with $N(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that every 1–3 tree of order $n$ contains at least $\alpha N$ distinct leaf-to-leaf path lengths between $0$ and $N$. The source gives upper and lower bounds with different exponents for this short-length problem, so the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Francesco Di Braccio, Kyriakos Katsamaktsis, Jie Ma, Alexandru Malekshahian and Ziyuan Zhao, “Leaf-to-leaf paths and cycles in degree-critical graphs”, arXiv:2504.11656 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11656

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2025). “Their conjecture, however, was disproven by Narins, Pokrovskiy, and Szab\'o who showed that there are arbitrarily large degree 3-critical graphs with no cycle of length 23.”

object.title: Signless Laplacian supersaturation conjecture for cliques
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $q(G)$ denote its signless Laplacian spectral radius. For fixed $k\geq 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, consider graphs whose signless Laplacian spectral radius exceeds the threshold $2(1-1/k)n$. **Signless Laplacian supersaturation conjecture.** If $k\geq 3$ is fixed and $n$ is sufficiently large, then

$$
q(G)>\left(1-\frac{1}{k}\right)2n
$$

for an $n$-vertex graph $G$ implies that $G$ contains at least

$$
\left(\frac{n}{k}\right)^{k-1}+O(n^{k-2})
$$

copies of $K_{k+1}$. This would provide a signless-Laplacian analogue of clique supersaturation, while the paper notes that the corresponding assertion for triangles fails and that the conjecture differs from the stronger linear-margin supersaturation theorem.
object.source_name: Jian Zheng, Yongtao Li and Yi-Zheng Fan, “Some Turán-type results for the signless Laplacian spectral radius”, arXiv:2507.02263 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02263

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2025).

object.title: Conlon–Luo–Tyomkyn's monochromatic component edge conjecture
object.statement:
Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers with $r\ge 3$, and let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices whose edges are colored with $r$ colors. A **monochromatic connected component** is a connected component in the subgraph formed by the edges of one color. **Conlon–Luo–Tyomkyn's conjecture.** Every such coloring contains a monochromatic connected component with at least

$$
\frac{1}{r(r-1)}\binom{n}{2}
$$

edges. This would match the upper bound supplied by Gyárfás's construction for infinitely many values of $r$, including whenever $r-1$ is a prime power; the cases $r=3$ and $r=4$ are known, while the assertion for general $r$ remains open.
object.source_name: Hannah Fox and Sammy Luo, “Monochromatic components with many edges in random graphs”, arXiv:2509.01766 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01766

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

object.title: Nonexistence of almost-complete Harary polynomials
object.statement:
Let $\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)$ be the random graph model with edge probability $1/2$, and let a Harary polynomial be a graph polynomial arising from a graph property. A graph polynomial is **almost complete** when asymptotically almost all graphs in the model are uniquely determined by it.

**Harary almost-completeness conjecture.** There is no Harary polynomial which is almost complete for $\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)$.

This is proposed in contrast with the Bollobás–Pebody–Riordan conjecture for the chromatic polynomial. The supplied text gives no resolution or supporting theorem for this stronger nonexistence claim.
object.source_name: Johann A. Makowsky, “Distinctive power and comparability of Harary polynomial”, arXiv:2512.22556 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22556

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

object.title: The ordinary-flat conjecture for complex-representable matroids
object.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, and call a rank-$k$ flat **ordinary** if it is the direct sum of a point and a rank-$(k-1)$ flat. **Ordinary-flat conjecture.** For each integer $k\ge 2$, every complex-representable matroid with rank at least $k+2$ has an ordinary rank-$k$ flat. This conjectures the complex-representable analogue of Hansen's theorem for real-representable matroids. Bounds of order $\Omega(k)$ were previously known, and the paper proves the weaker bound $4(k-1)$; the conjectured bound remains open.
object.source_name: Jim Geelen and Matthew E. Kroeker, “A Sylvester-Gallai-type theorem for complex-representable matroids”, arXiv:2212.03307 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.03307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
